svg.text: The talk is a funnel: scattered failed beliefs narrow into one diagnosis (Cargo Cult Science) and one rule
(scientific integrity), which is then worked out point by point and tested against real cases, before a closing
line loops back to that same rule.

g.text: Broad hunting for beliefs that don't work funnels into naming the problem and its missing rule; that rule is worked out
in a chain of points, tested against a chain of real cases, then the closing wish loops back to it.

g.title: Mysticism, ESP, Geller: nothing worked — Isolation tanks, Esalen, reflexology, and Uri Geller's key-bending all failed under Feynman's own look. — → spya-q4502k
Education and crime 'science' show no progress — Reading scores and crime rates stay flat despite decades of expert methods, like an unchecked witch-doctor remedy. — → spya-aww976
A test for spotting fields nobody understands — Any topic safe to discuss loudly at a cocktail party is one nobody actually has a handle on. — → spya-wc4h5s
Named: Cargo Cult Science — Like islanders who build fake runways and control towers, the form of science is followed but no planes land. — → spya-fd2muf
Core rule: report what counts against you — Leaning-over-backwards honesty: report everything that might make your own result wrong. — → spya-afgs74
Unlike ads, give the whole truth — "Wesson Oil doesn't soak through food" is true but misleading — no oil does, at the right temperature. — → spya-bpyx8n
g.text: Unlike ads, give the whole truth

g.title: Careless work is eventually found out — Other experimenters repeat the work; a hard subject is not an excuse for Cargo Cult Science. — → spya-az6z7k
g.text: Careless work is eventually found out

g.title: Millikan's error crept toward truth too slowly — Later measurements of the electron's charge inched upward instead of jumping straight to the right value. — → spya-s9msxy
g.text: Millikan's error crept toward truth too

g.title: First rule: you fool yourself easiest — That slow creep happened because researchers distrusted results too far from Millikan's, not too close. — → spya-bvx2u8
g.text: First rule: you fool yourself easiest

g.title: Owe laymen the same honesty — A scientist should admit on the radio that a line of research has no practical use, even if funding suffers. — → spya-c46yyu
Publish every result, win or lose — Advice to a senator, or a cigarette's test results, must be published whichever way the answer comes out. — → spya-jk7mj4
g.text: Publish every result, win or lose

g.title: Psychology and physics both skip needed repeats — A student was told not to replicate a prior rat experiment; a physics lab likewise skipped a comparison run. — → spya-w9nnq6
Young's careful rat clues, later ignored — Young eliminated every false clue a rat could use in a maze, yet later rat studies never used his method. — → spya-fvenms
Rhine's ESP effects shrink toward zero — As parapsychology tightened its controls, its measured effects kept getting smaller and smaller. — → spya-rbpppq
Final wish: keep your integrity — Feynman's closing wish: the freedom to keep this integrity without institutional pressure to drop it. — → spya-ndyj3t

g.text: A straight chain: name the failure, state the rule of integrity, then draw out what that rule demands — in evidence, in
a real case of self-deception, and in honesty toward the public and policymakers.

g.title: Cargo Cult Science: the form of science, nothing works — Like fake airstrips built by islanders waiting for planes that never come. — → spya-fd2muf
Missing piece: report what counts against you — A kind of leaning-over-backwards honesty, not explicitly taught, only caught by example. — → spya-afgs74
Advertising twists truth by implication, not lies — "Wesson Oil doesn't soak through food" is true, but implies something false about oils in general. — → spya-bpyx8n
g.text: Advertising twists truth by implication, not

g.title: Careless work is eventually exposed — Other experimenters repeat it, and nature itself will agree or disagree with a sloppy theory. — → spya-az6z7k
Millikan's electron charge was slightly off, and fixes crept in slowly — Each new measurement nudged the value up only a little, instead of jumping straight to the right number. — → spya-s9msxy
g.text: Millikan's electron charge was slightly off,

g.title: That slow creep shows: you fool yourself first — Researchers distrusted results far from Millikan's and didn't look hard at results close to it. — → spya-bvx2u8
g.text: That slow creep shows: you fool yourself

g.title: Scientists owe laymen the same honesty — Even admitting on the radio that cosmology research has no practical use, rather than claiming one to keep funding. — → spya-c46yyu
g.text: Scientists owe laymen the same honesty

g.title: Publish every result, not just the favorable one — Whether testing a cigarette's nicotine or advising a senator on drilling, both outcomes must see print. — → spya-jk7mj4
g.text: Publish every result, not just the favorable
Testing the rule against real cases
A chain of examples where the rule is skipped or kept, each with its telling aside, ending in the clearest failure and

g.title: Psychology rarely repeats its own experiments — A student proposed changing one condition of a prior rat study without first re-running the original. — → spya-w9nnq6
Her professor: don't repeat it, that's a waste of time — The 1935 policy was to change conditions and see what happens, never to re-check the original result. — → spya-v0xcd7
A physics lab skipped a needed comparison run too — Pressure for new results meant a deuterium experiment borrowed someone else's mismatched hydrogen data instead. — → spya-m95kqm
g.text: A physics lab skipped a needed

g.title: Young ruled out every false clue in his rat maze — He painted doors, masked smells, covered the corridor, and finally sanded the floor to kill every giveaway. — → spya-fvenms
g.text: Young ruled out every false clue in his

g.title: Later researchers ignored his careful method entirely — No one cited his controls or his sand-covered corridor; rat studies went back to the old sloppy way. — → spya-wye8g6
As ESP tests got stricter, Rhine's effects shrank to nothing — Every fix to the method made the measured effect smaller, yet it was still called a repeatable result. — → spya-rbpppq
g.text: As ESP tests got stricter, Rhine's

g.title: His fix: train only students who already get results — A parapsychology institute's outgoing director advised dropping students who only scored by chance. — → spya-g203mu
g.text: His fix: train only students who

g.title: Feynman's wish: freedom to keep your integrity — A closing wish that no need for funding or standing should force you to give up that honesty. — → spya-ndyj3t
